correctness.rationale: The centered regular simplex has barycentric inequalities v_i·x>=-1/n, so intersecting with its negative gives the exact symmetric slab system |v_i·x|<=1/n. Central symmetry moves every inscribed Euclidean ball to the origin, proving r=1/n. The tight-frame identity converts squared norm exactly to the squared l2 norm of the zero-sum cube coordinates y_i=n v_i·x divided by n(n+1). Strict convexity reduces the maximum to cube-section vertices. Parity then forces either balanced +/-1 coordinates or one zero plus balanced +/-1 coordinates, proving the two circumradii and all equality cases.
risks: The finite verifier checks only dimensions through 10; the proof for all dimensions is the exact extreme-point argument, not the computation.

value.rationale: The body S∩(-S) is the canonical centrally symmetric kernel of the simplex and is singled out in a classical symmetry problem and in Brannen's projection-body extremal program. Its Euclidean roundness is therefore a motivated geometric invariant. The theorem gives a complete all-dimensional metric profile, including a genuine parity transition and every farthest point, rather than a single small-dimensional computation.
risks: The result is a structural benchmark for the canonical kernel; it does not settle the surrounding projection-body extremal conjecture.
